clue.text: One's hooked on Carthage when touring

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the letters of these two words wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller is gripped by the ancient city of Carthage while visiting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's hooked on' reads as 'someone is addicted to', but the definition stops at 'hooked': the thing that hangs from a hook in a wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe hanger is shaped to hang by its hook from a rail, so it is the thing that is hooked.

clue.text: Mineworkers' lift, a hundred years old?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
age is how many years old someone or something is

explanation.surface: Asks whether the lift taking miners down the shaft is a century old.
explanation.definitionFit: In mining, the enclosed platform that carries workers up and down the shaft is called the cage.

clue.text: Court order investigations finally into all blood groups?

indicators.note: into says the single letter goes inside the blood-group letters

parts.note: the ABO system names the main human blood groups A, B, AB and O

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word investigations

explanation.surface: A court orders tests on everyone's blood type after an investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was an Anti-Social Behaviour Order, a British court order restricting a nuisance's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation names a specific kind of UK court order imposed for antisocial conduct.

clue.text: Last part of race perhaps flat and neat

parts.note: a flat is perhaps someone's home, an example of one
a neat drink is served straight, undiluted

explanation.surface: The end of a race run perhaps on a flat, tidy course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks a flat as just one kind of home.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stretch of a racecourse leading to the winning post is its closing straight run.

clue.text: Endlessly drink something sticky, sugary fluid

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for drink loses its final letter

parts.note: to neck a drink is to swallow it quickly, British slang
tar is a thick sticky black substance

explanation.surface: Someone keeps drinking a sticky, sugary syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like it means 'constantly' but trims NECK to NEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers produce a sweet liquid that bees collect to make honey.

clue.text: Some disgrace, yes, or especially hideous sights

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grumble that some things are a disgrace, especially ugly ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly buildings or views that offend the eye are commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Book entering system, marked

indicators.note: entering says the answer sits inside the run of clue words that follow

explanation.surface: A library book being logged into a cataloguing system and marked.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Austen's novel of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel about a matchmaking heroine is a well-known book of that title.

clue.text: I came with him, a drunk, around British resort city

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters go round the single letter
drunk means tipsy and muddled, so these letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone arrived with a tipsy companion at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges I CAME HIM A into MIAMIEACH; 'around' puts it round B.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida city on a barrier island is a famous beach resort.

clue.text: Everyone repeat, inking in identical initials?

definitions.note: the -ing phrase stands for the verb: writing words that start with matching letters

parts.note: all means everyone
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: An instruction for everybody to repeat something while writing matching initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to use a series of words beginning with the same sound, as in a playful phrase.

clue.text: Surprised when kissed on the lips?

definitions.meaning: astounded, utterly amazed, in British slang
a gob is slang for mouth and a smack is a loud kiss, so a mouth that got smacked

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone was taken aback by a kiss on the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: GOB is British slang for mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang word for astounded literally pictures a mouth that has been struck.

clue.text: Post for a chap under discussion

indicators.note: something under discussion is being spoken about, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a chap is a male person

explanation.surface: A job opening for a man is being talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters and parcels delivered by the postal service are the post.

clue.text: Cook taking sort of utensil for warming marshmallows?

indicators.note: to cook something up is to concoct it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cook picking a kind of utensil to heat marshmallows over a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled fork for holding bread to a fire also serves to warm marshmallows, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Might one have got tied up at work?

definitions.text: Might one have got tied up at work?

parts.words: Might one have got tied up at work?
parts.note: being tied up at work usually means being busy, but a performer who escapes from ropes and chains is literally bound as part of the act

explanation.definitionFit: An escape artist like Houdini is bound in ropes or chains as part of the performance.

clue.text: Old part of clock

definitions.meaning: the pointer that marks the seconds on a clock face

explanation.definitionFit: Goods already owned before are pre-used; the clock pointer that sweeps once a minute shares the name.

clue.text: Around middle of autumn, at last we reviewed a kind of legislation

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters go round the middle pair
reviewed suggests the words have been gone over and reworked into a new order
middle of picks the central two letters of the word autumn

explanation.surface: In mid-autumn the last items are finally reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' turns AT LAST WE into STATELAW; 'Around' wraps that round TU, the middle of 'autumn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Law passed by a legislature, as opposed to common law, is the parliamentary kind.

clue.text: Edges of Egyptian flag complete

indicators.note: edges of picks the first and last letters of the word Egyptian

parts.note: to flag is to tire or weaken

explanation.surface: The borders of an Egyptian flag are complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole, with nothing missing, is a synonym of complete.

clue.text: Cryptic answer by the setter in trousers, etc

definitions.note: a list of items standing for the collective noun for clothing

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and obscure, so the letters of the word are disguised in a new order

explanation.surface: A setter offers a cryptic solution listing trousers and similar.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers and the like are examples of clothing sold for men.

clue.text: Short let written about in flier

indicators.note: written about suggests the letters are scribbled around into a new order

explanation.surface: A brief rental is described in a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' looks like a printed leaflet; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The song thrush, a bird, is called by this old name; a flier is anything that flies.

clue.text: Total on strike correct

parts.note: workers on strike are out
correct means right

explanation.surface: Every worker is out on strike, and rightly so.
explanation.definitionFit: An outright win is a total, complete one.

clue.text: Tiger perhaps a bit upset about getting caught, initially

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the picked pair
upset means knocked over, so these letters are tipped into a new order
initially picks the first letter of each of the words getting and caught

explanation.surface: A tiger is somewhat put out at being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns A BIT into BIAT; 'about' wraps it round GC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigers, lions and leopards are examples of the large wild felines.

clue.text: Shrub with blight in seed

indicators.note: in says one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a pea is a seed
rot is decay or blight

explanation.surface: A bush is infected with disease spreading into its seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African flowering shrub with large showy heads is a protea, a genus name.

clue.text: Spirit from the bottle?

parts.note: spirit means both bravery and strong drink, so this is boldness found in alcohol

explanation.definitionFit: Boldness gained by drinking alcohol is the idiomatic name for bravery from drink.

clue.text: European capitals in Sweden, Estonia, Russia and Belgium

indicators.note: capitals here are the initial capital letters of the country names, not their capital cities

explanation.surface: A list of the capital cities of four European countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' suggests Stockholm or Tallinn, but means the initial capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Serbia is a European.

clue.text: Write category

definitions.meaning: to put words down using a keyboard

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means writing on a keyboard; the noun means a kind or sort.

clue.text: Hiding head, fool friend

indicators.note: hiding head means the first letter of the word is concealed and dropped

parts.note: to dally is to fool around or trifle

explanation.surface: Someone conceals their face to trick a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner who supports you is a friend; nations on the same side are this too.

clue.text: Writing stuff fixed, by the sound of it

indicators.note: says the word is heard, so a word spelt differently but said the same is entered

parts.note: fixed in place means not moving

explanation.surface: Writing materials apparently already sorted out.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper, envelopes and pens are the materials used for writing.

clue.text: Sad — unlike this clue?

definitions.meaning: this clue is an across clue, and its opposite direction in the grid names the other kind

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low is a common synonym for sad; the grid direction opposite to across is the other sense.

clue.text: Regarding ruin, bleak winds extraordinary

parts.note: re means regarding or about
to mar is to spoil or ruin

indicators.note: winds as a verb means twists, so the letters of the word are twisted round

explanation.surface: On the subject of devastation, bleak winds are extraordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' looks like gusts of air but is the verb, twisting BLEAK into KABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthy of remark is striking and unusual.
